$comment: Canonical indicator store. Editable three ways: directly in this file, through the lightweight admin screen at /admin, or by CSV/Excel ingest (npm run ingest). Values marked illustrative are shaped from published SUNCASA reporting and will be replaced from the SUNCASA data catalogue after contract signature. Source classes follow the RFP: FMES, SUNCASA monitoring, National, Public.

indicators.name_en: Area restored or under improved management
indicators.name_rw: Ubuso bwasubijwe ubuzima cyangwa bucungwa neza
indicators.provider: SUNCASA project team (IISD and WRI) with RFA
indicators.definition_en: Total hectares in the six lower Nyabarongo micro-catchments where afforestation, reforestation, riparian restoration, terracing, or improved management has been implemented under SUNCASA.
indicators.why_en: Restored land holds rainfall instead of shedding it. Every hectare brought under restoration or improved management reduces the flood and erosion pressure on the communities living downstream.
indicators.caveats_en: Illustrative composite of published Year 2 agroforestry (1,654 ha) and riparian buffer (362 ha) figures. The data catalogue may define restored area differently, so this number will be replaced after validation.

indicators.provider: SUNCASA project team (IISD and WRI) with RFA
indicators.definition_en: Hectares of riverbank vegetation restored along the Nyabarongo and its tributaries to stabilise banks, filter runoff, and slow floodwater.
indicators.why_en: The strip of vegetation beside a river is its first line of defence. A restored buffer keeps soil out of the water, slows floods, and gives wildlife a corridor through the city.
indicators.caveats_en: Published Year 2 figure equal to 92 percent of target. Subject to validation against the data catalogue.

indicators.source: National risk mapping and SUNCASA environmental monitoring
indicators.provider: Rwanda Water Resources Board with SUNCASA project team
indicators.definition_en: Coverage of flood and erosion risk context mapping across the six SUNCASA micro-catchments, shown as map layers on the intervention map.
indicators.why_en: Risk maps turn scattered flood memories into a shared picture. They show why interventions sit where they sit, and they help residents and planners see the same problem the same way.
indicators.caveats_en: Risk extents on the prototype map are illustrative placeholders. Approved layers will be consumed from national sources in WGS84 with the ITRF2005 transformation documented.

indicators.provider: SUNCASA project team (IISD and WRI) with RFA and City of Kigali
indicators.definition_en: Cumulative number of trees and buffer plants reported under SUNCASA in Kigali across afforestation, reforestation, agroforestry, riparian, and urban planting activities.
indicators.why_en: Trees are the most visible promise of this programme. Counting them honestly, and following whether they survive, is how a promise becomes a forest.
indicators.caveats_en: Published Year 2 cumulative of trees and buffer plants. Survival rates are tracked separately and are not shown in this MVP.

indicators.provider: SUNCASA project team (IISD and WRI) with RFA
indicators.definition_en: Hectares of farmland where trees have been integrated with crops under SUNCASA agroforestry support, combining production with soil protection.
indicators.why_en: Agroforestry feeds families while it holds the hillside together. It is where the environmental story and the livelihood story become the same story.
indicators.caveats_en: Published Year 2 figure, more than 450 hectares ahead of the published target. Subject to validation against the data catalogue.

indicators.source: Satellite-derived vegetation index over intervention areas
indicators.definition_en: Change in vegetated area across the six micro-catchments relative to the pre-intervention baseline, derived from publicly available satellite imagery.
indicators.why_en: Satellites do not exaggerate. An independent, repeatable measure of green cover lets the programme show change that anyone can verify.
indicators.caveats_en: Proposed indicator with an illustrative value. Method, baseline year, and data readiness to be confirmed during inception.

indicators.definition_en: Water quality in the lower Nyabarongo, included only if a data-ready national series is confirmed during inception, as the PRD anticipates.
indicators.why_en: Cleaner water is one of the quietest benefits of restoration. If a credible national series exists, the dashboard will show it rather than estimate it.
indicators.caveats_en: Proposed indicator with no value shown. The PRD includes water quality only if data-ready. No new data collection under the MVP.

indicators.provider: SUNCASA project team with AVEGA Agahozo and partners
indicators.definition_en: Number of women and members of marginalized groups actively engaged in SUNCASA restoration activities, governance structures, and consultations.
indicators.why_en: SUNCASA is a gender-responsive programme by design. Making participation visible keeps that commitment honest and shows that inclusion is an outcome, not a slogan.
indicators.caveats_en: Illustrative value. Final disaggregated figures come from the SUNCASA data catalogue and are validated before publication.

indicators.provider: SUNCASA project team with RYWP and partners
indicators.definition_en: Number of people trained under SUNCASA in nursery management, planting, terracing, agroforestry, and ecosystem stewardship.
indicators.why_en: Skills stay after the project ends. Training is how a two-year investment becomes a twenty-year capability in the watershed's own communities.
indicators.caveats_en: Illustrative value pending the data catalogue. Disaggregation by gender and age to be confirmed during inception.

indicators.definition_en: Jobs created through SUNCASA activities including nurseries, planting crews, terracing, and agroforestry, disaggregated by gender and age.
indicators.why_en: Green jobs make restoration self-interested, in the best way. When wages flow from the watershed's recovery, the watershed gains a workforce of defenders.
indicators.caveats_en: Illustrative value with illustrative disaggregation (58 percent women, 47 percent youth). Final figures come from validated SUNCASA reporting.
